title: Inflected Past Potential Modals: Verb + -hatott/-hetett volna

sections.title: Personal Agency vs. Impersonal Possibility
sections.content: You know *-hatott/-hetett volna* from B2 Unit 15; here you use it in the story of Semmelweis. Whereas lehetett volna + infinitive is impersonal ('one could have / it could have been done'), attaching the potential suffix -hat/-het directly to the verb in the past conditional (verb + -hatott/-hetett + personal ending + volna) attributes the missed capability or opportunity to a specific grammatical subject: Semmelweis hamarabb is publikálhatta volna az eredményeit ('Semmelweis could have published his results earlier').

sections.title: Definite vs. Indefinite Conjugation in Past Modals
sections.content: Because verb + -hatott/-hetett volna is a fully inflected finite verb, it obeys standard Hungarian transitivity agreement! Use the indefinite forms (tanulhattam volna, segíthetett volna) when there is no definite object, and the definite forms (meggyőzhette volna a kollégáit, átírhatták volna a történelmet) when there is a definite direct object.

sections.title: Past Potential (-hat/-het + Past + volna) Paradigm
rows: Semmelweis korábban is megírhatta volna a könyvét. (Def.)
Semmelweis could have written his book earlier.
A professzorok ellenőrizhették volna az adatokat. (Def.)
The professors could have verified the data.
The patients could have remained alive.
Semmelweis hamarabb is publikálhatta volna az eredményeit. (Def.)
Semmelweis could have published his results earlier.

items.spanish: Ha a korabeli orvosi kar nyitottabban fogadta volna az adatokat, évtizedekkel korábban átírhatták volna a kórházak történetét.
items.english: If the contemporary medical faculty had received the data more openly, they could have rewritten the history of hospitals decades earlier.

items.spanish: Ha Semmelweis nyugodt hangnemben válaszolt volna a kétkedőknek, könnyebben meggyőzhette volna a nemzetközi közvéleményt.
items.english: If Semmelweis had answered the skeptics in a calm tone, he could have convinced international opinion more easily.

items.spanish: A főorvosok megvizsgálhatták volna a kórházi statisztikákat, de nem tették meg.
items.english: The chief physicians could have examined the hospital statistics, but they did not.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: In a counterfactual about the past, both clauses take volna: Ha megírta volna a könyvet, könnyebben meggyőzhette volna őket. The plain past (Ha megírta a könyvet, ...) is a real past condition, and the present tense (megírja) refers to the present or the future.
